method: After freezing the decision and canonical record, returned to the official 2026–2027 regulations, the current withdrawal and successor package guidance, and the course planner evidence for each final paper. Rebuilt the credit groups and checked the preparation and research progression. Reconsidered workbook-supported course contributions and terms against the finished pair in a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The standard Dutch-language LAS BA illustrated here has 60 EC General Education: four named 7.5 EC core courses and 15 EC in each of science and social science because the main direction is in the humanities. The 2026–2027 programme-specific regulations require 67.5–105 EC in an approved direction, including a final paper of at least 7.5 EC and at least 30 EC at level 3. The former first-listed Film and Television Studies direction was discontinued. The official successor is Media Industries, Identities and Heritage. Doing Media Heritage supplies 30 EC at level 3. Add the 7.5 EC media research preparation, one 7.5 EC introductory film or television preparation, the 7.5 EC research seminar, the 7.5 EC final paper and 7.5 EC of approved complementary main-direction study to reach the LAS minimum of 67.5 EC. This is an illustrative approved-choice structure, and the individual elective remains open. Profiling is the remaining 52.5 EC. The portfolio has zero credit. Utrecht requires both the LAS interdisciplinary paper and the media final paper.

The first year begins with Schrijfacademie, Multidisciplinair project and General Education electives. The film introduction in Block 3 and media research preparation in Block 4 can precede the four advanced heritage courses in the next year. The main-direction seminar requires 22.5 advanced EC and expects at least three package courses passed, met by completing the package first. The media paper follows that seminar. The current package explicitly pairs ME3V26011 and ME3V15026 despite the legacy seminar identifier on the thesis planner. The LAS paper follows De denkacademie and 120 earned EC. The two papers can be taken in separate Year 3 blocks, with required electives and profiling arranged around the preparation and media package.

The three options sustain media and society, environment and public policy, and digital society and AI as separate organising directions. UCR offers substantive courses for media analysis and documentary but no equivalent of the specific Utrecht package and both required final papers. The academic gaps and approved-choice structure are visible in the comparison.
